title: station/service@1
description: What every docked service answers to `station_describe`, what each operation answers, and what a task's `status`, `cancel` and `content` answer. An operation's arguments are the input schema it declares. See service-v1.md. Also checked by Station, beyond this schema: (1) Station counts a string's length in UTF-8 bytes where the contract says bytes, and otherwise in UTF-16 code units; the schema counts characters at the same bound, so a string with characters outside ASCII can pass the schema and still be too long. (2) Text a service writes for people or a model to read also holds no tag character (U+E0000 to U+E007F) and no lone surrogate; the `pattern` covers the rest of that rule. (3) No object anywhere in the answer holds a `__proto__`, `constructor` or `prototype` key, and nothing nests deeper than 40 levels (an opaque object, 32). (4) When `models` is given, `model` is not null and is one of `models`, and no two models share the label `provider/model`. (5) Each operation's `input_schema` serializes to at most 16384 UTF-8 bytes. (6) Each record's `fields` serializes to at most 16384 UTF-8 bytes. (7) Each derived entry's `content` serializes to at most 16384 UTF-8 bytes. (8) A step's `content` serializes to at most 65536 UTF-8 bytes. (9) A record carries at most 64 fields. (10) Declarations fit together: operation names are listed once and none is `describe`, `status`, `cancel` or `content`; each example names a listed operation; a service with a task gives `reporting_interval_seconds` and answers `status` and `cancel`, and a service with none gives null and no task calls. (11) Each `input_schema` is an object schema with `additionalProperties: false`, holding at its top level only `type`, `properties`, `required`, `additionalProperties`, `title` and `description`; `required` is a list of properties it lists; it lists properties exactly when the operation takes `args`. (12) `kinds` is given exactly when the operation gives back `records`; `target` exactly when it changes `target`, naming a required input property that is a typed id: a string with a `pattern` anchored by `^` and `$` and a `maxLength` of at most 256 (and no other keyword but `minLength`, `title` and `description`), or an object of nothing but required ones. (13) An operation that gives back `derived` takes `handed` or calls back; `spends.reports` is `answer` for an operation that runs `now` and `status` for a `task`. (14) An answer is for the operation called; it carries `result` for an operation that runs `now` and `task` for a `task`; its result's `gives` is the one the operation declared; each record is of a declared kind and no ref repeats; each derived entry names only items Station handed over in this call, each once; `spend` is given exactly when the operation spends. (15) A status is for the task asked about: no step id repeats and each `parent` comes earlier; a step or task has `failure` exactly when it failed; `waiting_on` only on a waiting step, and a waiting task has one; `result` exactly when it succeeded, fitting the declaration, and records in it carry no `next_cursor`; each decision's `step` is a reported step and its `about` names only items handed over; `spend` exactly when the operation spends. (16) A step label is one line. A `cancel` answer is for the task asked about; a `content` answer is for the task and step asked about, and is asked only of a service whose `task_calls` lists `content`. (17) In place of a result, any tool may answer the shared error answer, `errors.schema.json`.
